items.title: CAN bus turns stepper motors into daisy-chained, addressable units
items.why: One ESP32+driver board per motor, chained like RGB LEDs over CAN - build multi-axis rigs with way fewer wires.

items.title: A hobbyist built a USB graphics card from a single microcontroller chip
items.why: One $0.20 chip plus PCB-etched USB/RCA jacks makes a working video output - a lesson in doing more with less silicon.

items.title: Someone let an AI model steer a llama.cpp fork tuned for old AMD GPUs
items.why: GLM wrote tile kernels and a mixed-GPU split mode for ancient Radeon VIIs - real speed claims, but unverified by others yet.

items.title: A paper rethinks LLM agent caching: match structure, not meaning
items.why: Splits requests into action+target instead of embeddings, fixing why semantic caches confuse 'check email' with 'send email.'

items.title: A hacker reverse-engineered custom firmware for a locked RF test instrument
items.why: Custom firmware adds ham-radio tools and remote access to a locked-down cellular test analyzer - real hacking, not open source.

items.title: Union-Find gets an undo button: the trick behind offline dynamic connectivity
items.why: DSU with rollback plus a segment tree over time turns edge deletions into a solvable offline problem - a real CF differentiator.

items.title: eBPF tools see Linux I/O that top and htop never show you
items.why: opensnoop-bpfcc and a one-line bpftrace probe watch kernel events live instead of sampling /proc - try it on your box today.

items.title: Reframing interview nerves as excitement actually improves performance
items.why: Saying 'I am excited' before a speech, math test or karaoke beat trying to stay calm in 3 real experiments - say it before you walk in.

items.title: A small trial found creatine loading boosted sprints, not clearly sleep or focus
items.why: 14-man RCT: sprint distance jumped clearly, but sleep and focus gains rest on one self-reported measure each - stay skeptical.

items.title: Getting sunlight before 10am was linked to earlier, better sleep
items.why: A survey of 1,762 adults found more morning light tracked with an earlier sleep midpoint - plausible, not yet proven causal.
items.source: PsyPost, on Menezes-Junior et al. (BMC Public Health)
